title: Moving a Personal Sender Account Down a Level When a Required Document Lapses
content:
When a document the current level of a Personal Sender Account requires lapses — a government ID passes its expiry date — and no accepted replacement is logged, the account moves down only once the level's lapse grace in calendar days has passed since the document's expiry date. Grace days are counted in calendar days from the expiry date, so the downgrade takes effect on the expiry date plus the grace days.

## The level moved down to

The new level is the current level's move-down level. When that level also requires the lapsed document, the step repeats from that level until a level is reached whose requirements are all met. The date the new level took effect is the downgrade date, and the next periodic review due date is recalculated for the new level.

## Effect on transfers

Transfers already booked keep their booking; new bookings use the lower limits and funding methods.

## Replacement documents

- An accepted replacement logged before the grace period ends cancels the downgrade.
- One logged after the grace period ends allows a new upgrade under the agent-applied upgrade rule.

## Boundary (hypothetical dates)

An account at Paloma Enhanced, whose lapse grace is 30 calendar days, has its only government ID expire on 1 May with no accepted replacement logged. The downgrade takes effect on 31 May (1 May plus 30 days), not on 30 May. Because the level moved down to, Paloma Verified Plus, also requires a government ID, the step repeats from Paloma Verified Plus, and again from Paloma Verified, until Paloma Starter, which requires no government ID, is reached.
